items.item: The Data Vault Model is a detail-oriented, historical-tracking, uniquely linked set of normalized tables, a hybrid of 3NF and star schema

at.step: Same domain, three models, one question

items.item: Hubs contain business keys with low propensity to change and no descriptive attributes

at.step: Reveal: hubs

items.item: Links capture the relationship between hubs, with the participating hub keys defining the grain

at.step: Reveal: links

items.item: Satellites contain descriptive attributes and their history, append-only so every change is preserved

at.step: Reveal: satellites

items.item: Data is never deleted from the data vault, unless there is a technical error while loading data

at.step: Reveal: what the join cost actually buys

items.item: Since hubs, links and satellites are only joined through links, each can be loaded in parallel

at.step: Predict: can separate loaders run with no coordinator?

items.item: A deterministic hash key can replace a sequence-generated surrogate key; every loader using the same key definition derives the identical key independently

at.step: Reveal: hash keys make it safe, computed

items.item: Generated surrogate keys force a child loader to look up the parent's stored key first, creating load-order dependencies that a deterministic hash key removes

at.step: Reveal: why a sequence could not do this

items.item: PIT structures identify the applicable satellite records for selected snapshot times; bridge structures simplify multi-join paths across commonly traversed hubs and links

at.step: Reveal: bridge tables, for the other kind of cost

items.item: Join performance improves with fixed-length hash keys; parallel loading becomes simpler because processes can independently generate identical hash values without coordinating

at.step: Reveal: hash keys make it safe, computed

items.item: PIT tables pre-materialize temporal joins across multiple satellites at load time rather than query time

at.step: Reveal: a point-in-time table cuts it back down, measured

items.item: Bridge tables flatten complex link structures, such as a path through five links, for common query patterns

at.step: Reveal: bridge tables, for the other kind of cost
